newsitem.title: USA: Roth urges Clinton, Congress to look at CPI now.
newsitem.headline: Roth urges Clinton, Congress to look at CPI now.

text.p: Senate Finance Committee chairman William Roth on Wednesday urged the White House and lawmakers to carefully study adjusting the consumer price index, based on a report being released today.
"I think it deserves careful attention immediately," the Delaware Republican said on CNN TV's "Early Edition".

He was speaking ahead of the release of a report by a Senate-appointed bipartisan commission which is expected to say that inflation, as measured by the Consumer Price Index, has been overstated by 1.1 percent and should be adjusted downward.
"What I'm interested in doing now with these recommendations of the commission is to develop a broad consensus," Roth said.
Lowering inflation estimates would lower federal benefits programs, such as Social Security, and tax brackets which are tied to the cost of living index.
"Nothing is going to get done unless we have bipartisan support for change, and that in turn means we need leadership from the president," Roth said.
Boskin told reporters the report would include recommendations for legislation.
"What is being proposed are changes that, for example, could extend Social Security another 20 years," Roth said.
The Clinton administration has said that it would be unable to change the CPI calculation in time for the fiscal 1998 budget negotiations.
